$comment: Architectural fitness rules for titan-platform, run by codewatch's `graph check` (scripts/dag-check.sh). The package-layers rule IS the platform DAG: a package may import only packages in the same tier or a lower one. `$tiers` is the source of truth (edited by scripts/new-package.mjs); `layers` is derived from it by dropping empty tiers, because codewatch rejects empty layers.

packages/code-graph/src/history imports nothing from the rest of code-graph, so a later extraction into @titan-design/git-history is a directory move. The rest of code-graph may import history.
The metric catalogue imports only its own directory and types.ts, so a browser-safe subpath can re-export it without pulling in ts-morph, tree-sitter, or SQLite.
Node builtins would break the catalogue in a browser.
rpc-client's main entry ships to browsers; only src/node (exportSnapshot) may use Node builtins.
react-app's main entry ships to browsers; only src/vite (the build preset) may use Node builtins.
Vite is an optional peer for the ./vite entry; the hooks must load without it. The leading ** anchors the match so npm:vitest in tests stays allowed.
No library in titan-platform imports one from titan-design or the reverse; only products cross that line (site/guides/where-code-goes.md). Only products and apps may import @titan-design/react-ui.
No library in titan-platform imports one from titan-design or the reverse; only products cross that line (site/guides/where-code-goes.md). Only products and apps may import @titan-design/beats.

The video mechanism packages (frame-capture, render-qa, graph-layout, speech-*) run without React: pixels live in titan-design, and these hold engines with no pixels. One rule per package because codewatch globs have no braces; a glob that matches nothing, as render-qa does until it exists, is accepted.
